kiln_p04_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_001.text: The fresh sample firing began on a morning so cold that the charcoal keeper's moustache carried tiny white beads. Luo made the ordinary crew repeat the occupied-post warning check before lighting. The drying-room answer came clearly through its relay. Yue stood at the recording bench with a wool wrap over her shoulders and no live lead attached to her body. She knew the sample positions, the witness method and the path to the outer door. Everything she could prepare was prepared. The six cups still had to survive conditions that a cold plan could only describe.

kiln_p04_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_002.text: Zhu's retained samples looked plain through the inspection opening. Their measured walls were less graceful than the first drawing and still thinner than the association's reference cup. Today's trial would not certify them for a charge. It would establish ordinary firing behavior in the fresh body. Tan repeated that distinction to the purchaser's runner, who had arrived before dawn hoping to take a success note back by noon. The runner asked whether he should wait. Tan suggested breakfast. It was the first useful thing anybody could promise him before the kiln became hot.

kiln_p04_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_003.text: The first heat interval passed without an irregular reading. Han fed sound ordinary charcoal in the planned portions, keeping the screened crumbs for a different permitted use. Yue wrote each feed with its time and watched the witness tile through the rated opening. The supplemental measuring channel held within its tested range. She found herself relaxing too early. Luo noticed her hand leave the recording slate before the next observation. He asked what the present quiet proved. She answered that the present interval was quiet. He nodded, and she returned her hand to the work.

kiln_p04_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_004.text: Later, the tile on the lower left position changed faster than the matching upper witness. The difference lay near the permitted comparison boundary. Luo checked the ordinary reference and the position notes before altering anything. No one asked Yue to steady the kiln with her reserve. The machine had its own rated supply and a shutdown plan. They held the permitted interval while checking the air path from outside. A narrow outer vent was drawing unevenly as cold wind crossed the yard. Its position mark showed open; the actual moving air was not equally distributed.

kiln_p04_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_005.text: Luo could safely reduce the heating rate and continue the small trial, or close the firing early and lose its intended comparison. He selected the slower permitted programme already specified for a change in wind. The choice did not guarantee sound cups. It kept the live process within the known equipment condition. Jian relayed the new interval to the occupied post and repeated it back before writing. Tan watched the longer schedule appear on the slate. His face fell, but he did not call it unnecessary. The flame kept moving, indifferent to the noon runner.

kiln_p04_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_006.text: Yue felt an irrational sense that she had failed by recording a problem. The slant of the tile colour made her want to inspect again until it resembled the other side. Zhu came to the clear recording station and asked for the actual observation. Yue read it aloud. Hearing the words steadied her. They were not a judgment on her, the clay or Luo. They were information the crew needed while there was still a useful action available. Zhu left without a comforting speech. The next comparison belonged to the next interval, not to Yue's wish.

kiln_p04_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_007.text: The lower witness slowly returned toward the matched range under the altered rate. Its earlier difference remained part of the history. Luo did not erase it by celebrating the later reading. The heating phase completed within the revised permitted schedule. Tan informed the runner that no sample result would be available until cooling and inspection. The young messenger groaned because his employer paid the same road allowance regardless of waiting. Peng offered the visitor bench and meal rate, with the association authorising the extra day. He sent his own note instead of sleeping cold in the gate.

kiln_p04_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_008.text: During the first cooling interval, the kiln clicked more loudly than Yue expected. Han said one particular sharp sound came from the outer brick seam, which had moved that way for years. He could not identify every sound inside. They used the planned witnesses rather than opening the hot door to satisfy curiosity. Yue stood farther from the wall than she had at the cold setup. Heat travelled through ordinary brick as well as measured channels. Her face flushed while her back stayed cold, a bodily contradiction no realm title made more comfortable.

kiln_p04_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_009.text: The night handover took place beside the clear bench. Jian explained the wind adjustment and showed where the revised rate began. The incoming worker repeated the key intervals and the warning response. Luo remained for the part requiring his oversight, while Yue's assigned observation ended at its proper time. She wanted to stay until everything cooled. Peng asked whether another exhausted observer would improve the result. Yue admitted she would mainly be trying to control the waiting. She went upstairs, washed the smoke from her hair and discovered that even her pillow seemed to smell of charcoal.

kiln_p04_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_010.text: She slept badly despite leaving on time. Dreaming made the lower witness permanently pale while everyone waited for her to name a colour. At dawn she reported the poor night and kept her route maintenance modest, with no increased admission. The clinic review was not due that morning, so she simply recorded the condition for the next scheduled check. Zhu said the dreams would probably become less original with experience. Han claimed his kiln dreams now consisted mostly of searching for a clean ladle. Yue preferred that possibility to being heroic and wrong all night.

kiln_p04_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_011.text: When the planned cooled inspection began, Luo checked the door's ordinary surface before allowing the crew inside. There was no hidden haste in the opening. Han lifted the nearest sample and smiled at its intact glaze. Then Zhu turned it so the lamp crossed the foot. A fine line followed the join between foot and wall. The second cup had a warped rim; the third looked sound under the first ordinary inspection. Yue's breath caught as the fourth revealed a similar foot line. Six careful samples could still produce a result nobody wanted to send.

kiln_p04_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_012.text: They placed each sample on its marked board rather than arranging the best-looking ones together. Two appeared sound under ordinary inspection, three showed foot or wall defects, and one had an uneven rim outside the proposed geometry. The apparently sound pair were retained for later checks, not announced as charged teaching vessels. Tan counted twice as if arithmetic might improve the shelf. Zhu asked him to copy the actual result. He did, his brush moving slowly. Luo took the firing slate from the wall and kept it beside the board where the cup positions could answer it.

kiln_p04_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_013.text: Yue found herself staring at the foot cracks. They were not identical. One followed a trimmed weak area; another lay beneath an apparently sound thickness. Zhu measured the cold walls with an ordinary tool and compared them with the retained forming notes. The body had behaved unevenly under the firing history. The crew could not yet assign all the faults to wind or maker. Luo proposed ordinary fracture inspection on one already failed sample, leaving the others intact for comparison. The owner approved the specimen use. Broken evidence would still have a recorded before state.

kiln_p04_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_014.text: Han cut the failed cup with a guarded ordinary tool at the cold bench. Yue watched the cross-section appear pale beneath the glaze. The centre contained no obvious fired reclaim particle like the prepared body's earlier failure. That helped distinguish the material histories without proving the fresh body perfect. The wall's interior had a small density difference near the foot. Zhu described how she had formed that join and where her hand pressure could have varied. She did not defend every movement because the cup carried her mark. A good maker could learn from an imperfect object she had made.

kiln_p04_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_015.text: Luo compared the two witnesses with the cup positions. The more rapidly changing lower interval explained some variation but not every fault. Their existing schedule came from an older reference body used in warmer conditions. It had been selected as a conservative starting programme, not a guarantee for this new vessel. The revised wind interval had remained within equipment safety, while the ceramic quality window might still have been too narrow. Yue wrote those separate conclusions carefully. A safe firing could produce unsound ware. Sound ware in one position could not absolve an unsuitable common schedule.

kiln_p04_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_016.text: The purchaser's runner waited beside the boards, trying not to look disappointed. He had expected six samples to tell his employer which drawing to approve. Instead he would carry a result requiring more development. Tan asked whether they could at least describe the two uncracked cups as accepted. Luo declined until the remaining ordinary checks and the method-specific bench test were complete. The runner sighed, then asked for the clearest report he could take. Yue helped make a simple position diagram. It was less flattering and easier to understand than a paragraph about promising preliminary performance.

kiln_p04_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_017.text: Peng priced the work needed to develop a second small trial. It included fresh sample preparation, ordinary fuel, a suitable reference comparison and the documentation time. Nobody entered the failed firing as free tuition for Yue merely because she had learned from it. The trial had served the commission's material question. Her wage remained wages. Tan examined the new cost and said the association would object. Peng said the objection would help them decide whether the larger commission was real. A purchaser could decline development without being sold a result that had not happened.

kiln_p04_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_018.text: Zhu took the failed samples downstairs herself. Yue offered to carry them as if relieving her of a humiliation. Zhu's expression changed. She asked whether Yue offered to carry every maker's failed work, or only hers. Yue heard the mistake at once. The trimmer was not helpless because a cup had cracked. Yue apologised and explained that she had seen the foot lines before understanding what they meant. Zhu accepted the apology but kept the tray. Their new friendship had not made every kind gesture wise. Yue went back to copy the cross-section measurements rather than managing someone else's disappointment.

kiln_p04_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_019.text: The quarrel stayed small because they let it remain honest. At lunch Yue sat beside Zhu rather than fleeing. She asked whether the failed shelf had hurt more after the credit correction. Zhu said it had hurt because she had wanted the clay to work. Her restored record was not a shield against caring about today's cup. Yue admitted wanting proof that the workshop's new care would be rewarded. Zhu broke a piece of bread and handed it over. Care improved the questions, she said. It could not bully the body into giving the answer they preferred.

kiln_p04_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_020.text: Jian had made no retained sample and still looked personally betrayed by the result. His record showed the correct assigned handover. The cups' defects did not erase that demonstrated task. Luo asked him to compare the revised interval with the older reference slate. The boy found where the wind adjustment began and where the lower position had changed earlier. He wanted to call the whole shelf a lesson. Luo said it was a failed material trial from which he could learn. The word failed belonged to the objects, not to every person who had touched the shift.

kiln_p04_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_021.text: Tan returned from the association office with a letter proposing that the two apparently sound cups be used for a private demonstration while the rest were remade. The demonstration would involve the brief charge described by the supplied method. Luo required the remaining ordinary vessel inspection before any charge, plus a rated grounded bench and the association's own instructor. A private room did not make an uninspected vessel safer. Tan read the condition to the agent directly, without turning it into an excuse blamed on Yue's caution. The agent reluctantly agreed to wait for the actual bench plan.

kiln_p04_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_022.text: Ordinary inspection found a fine glaze discontinuity in one of the apparent survivors under a changed lamp angle. The second remained sound under the specified cold checks. Zhu repeated the viewing method with Yue, showing how a bright reflection could cover rather than reveal a line. They retained both histories. The newly rejected cup would not be charged. The remaining cup could enter the limited bench evaluation, which still would not establish a four-hundred-vessel process. Yue felt her earlier count of two survivors shrink. The archive held the old count beside the inspection that corrected it.

kiln_p04_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_023.text: For the bench evaluation, the association sent its reference cup and an instructor with the documented method. The kiln owner funded the permitted small test charge and grounding wick as part of the commission work. Yue stayed an observer, her own reserve disconnected. The instructor first demonstrated interruption through the reference cup, then inspected the new sample at the cold bench. Its geometry differed at the foot and wall. The proposed modest load could be tested only under the guarded trial conditions, with no student holding it. The instructor agreed to that narrower question.

kiln_p04_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_024.text: The sound-looking sample accepted the first brief measured trace, but its release left a persistent surface warmth near the altered foot. The reference cup cleared sooner under the same permitted comparison. They stopped before trying another admission. The test charge came from the prepared supply and ended in the grounding wick; the remaining uncertainty belonged to the vessel's discharge behavior. Yue watched the instructor inspect the ordinary warmth after safe release. Nothing exploded. A dangerous difference could appear quietly enough that an eager maker might overlook it while celebrating the first successful light.

kiln_p04_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_025.text: Zhu said the sample was not acceptable for beginner instruction at that load and method. Tan wrote the refusal without asking whether a smaller class could use it. The instructor suggested that a different vessel geometry and release path might be developed, but would need its own material trial and guarded comparison. The association's reference design was not simply a decoration they could copy onto thinner walls. Yue thought of external conducting stitches, whose repair required new checks. A line could specify direction; ordinary backing still determined what the line could safely carry.

kiln_p04_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_026.text: Luo set the charged-tested cup apart with its discharge note. The trial had spent its small prepared charge, the wick's usable life and staff time. Those costs entered the commission account. No one recovered the charge by asking Yue to refill anything. Han looked at the cup and said it would make an excellent holder for sour pickles if ordinary use were cleared. Zhu said the glaze question would need consideration before food use. He sighed. Even retired vessels required honest work. They placed it among guarded study specimens, where its quiet failure could remain useful.

kiln_p04_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_027.text: The owner arrived late that afternoon. She was a broad-shouldered older woman who usually negotiated fuel and left Luo to the hall. She asked for the original proposal, the fresh material history and the failed shelf, not only the new cost estimate. Yue brought the packet and saw how Peng's plain index saved them from retelling the inquiry differently for each visitor. The owner listened, asked where her own purchase decision had been made and admitted she had approved too little development money. Her impatience had reached the clerk as another impossible deadline.

kiln_p04_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_028.text: She could not fund unlimited experimentation. The winter jar orders already owed their own fuel. She offered money for one carefully revised small ordinary trial after the association agreed to real geometry and demonstrated release conditions. Beyond that, they would renegotiate or decline the teaching commission. Luo accepted the limit as something he could plan within. Tan looked relieved and frightened at once. A finite useful trial was better than another vague demand for success, but declining the larger order might expose accounts he had hoped to keep moving until spring.

kiln_p04_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_029.text: Peng asked whether any advance on the four hundred teaching vessels had already been accepted. Tan hesitated, then produced an association receipt. The amount had entered a separate suspense account pending the sample decision. It had not yet bought fuel or paid ordinary wages. That restraint made return possible. The owner required the account balance checked and the advance kept untouched unless the commission was actually accepted. Yue saw Tan's relief sharpen into shame. He had wanted credit for being careful with the money without first admitting that the promised larger date had made its way onto the receipt.

kiln_p04_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_030.text: The receipt named a delivery month the kiln had never accepted. Tan had written it after a conversation relayed through association messengers, then failed to send the clause back for correction. Peng attached the earlier conditional estimate and requested an amended receipt. The owner would sign only the corrected terms. Yue did not confuse a disputed promise with a completed contract. She could see how the purchaser might have believed the date was real. Another error had become clearer because the sample failed before the unused advance disappeared into ordinary winter expenses.

kiln_p04_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_031.text: That night, Tan stayed after the hall closed to write the corrected answer. Yue passed his room on the way to return the lamp. He asked whether she thought he was a dishonest man. The question made her stop. She did not know his whole life. She knew the receipt should be corrected and the material instruction should have been read. Saying less than that would comfort him at somebody else's expense; saying more would pretend she could judge a person from two papers. He looked unhappy with the answer, but he did not call her cruel.

kiln_p04_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_032.text: She asked whether the month on the receipt had been his hope or the association's demand. He said it had begun as both and become his signature. His sister's letter lay beneath the unused string. He had promised family help after the expected order payment. Yue could understand why failure felt larger to him than six cups. She reminded him that the storage commission had paid honestly and that winter work might continue without the unproved teaching batch. He said honest small work did not always arrive when a large debt wanted it. Then he thanked her for listening.

kiln_p04_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_033.text: Yue left before the conversation became a request she could not safely satisfy. Upstairs she divided her own coins again, keeping travel money separate from ordinary purchases. She had enough to send home a modest share after the next completed wage block, not enough to repair every life in the hall. Her new fourth-stage skill did not make the choice effortless. She lay awake imagining a world in which helping one person could never leave another cost. In the morning that imagined world had done none of the ordinary work waiting downstairs.

kiln_p04_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_034.text: Zhu found her at the cold bench looking at the charged-tested cup. She asked whether Yue was planning to mend it with a better feeling. Yue smiled despite herself. The vessel's flaw lay in material, geometry and release behavior under the method. It needed redesign or retirement, not a practitioner's desire to be kind. They put the cup back in its guarded place and made two uncharged sketches. Zhu let Yue suggest a wider foot and a thicker lower wall. The next draft looked less graceful. It also looked more like something a beginner could hold without inheriting its weakness.

kiln_p04_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_035.text: Zhu kept the ugly new sketch pinned beside the graceful old one. Workers stopped to comment as they passed. Han preferred the wider foot because it looked less likely to argue with a table. Jian thought it resembled a duck sitting down. Luo asked whether a duck's lower wall could be measured. Tan said the purchaser would want to know why beauty had become optional. Zhu replied that they were designing a teaching vessel, not a seduction. Yue watched the two drawings become a conversation the entire hall could enter without pretending to be the final assessor.

kiln_p04_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_036.text: The comparison revealed another ordinary requirement. Beginner hands differed in size. A broad cup that felt secure to Luo could force a smaller learner to grip too hard. The association's reference vessel had a simple handle not shown in the first cheap drawing. Zhu made an uncharged wooden mock-up and asked workers to hold it. Jian's hand fitted; Yue's thumb strained against its edge. Han suggested moving the handle slightly instead of shrinking the whole vessel. They tested the changed mock-up again. No clay or prepared charge had been consumed to answer a question wood could answer first.

kiln_p04_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_037.text: Peng invited the association instructor back to inspect the uncharged mock-up and the written dimensional change. The instructor brought two adult learners whose ordinary grip differed visibly. Both knew they were evaluating shape, not attending a spiritual demonstration. One found the handle comfortable; the other caught a sleeve on its corner. Zhu rounded the corner in the wood and repeated the ordinary movement. Yue liked watching the learners alter an object that would eventually be called a teaching tool. They were neither a purchaser's abstract class nor bodies expected to adapt silently to a cheaper drawing.

kiln_p04_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_038.text: The instructor said the new geometry could enter material development if the release arrangement retained its rated clearance. She would not accept a guessed inscription copied from the failed sample. The association had to fund a suitable craft specialist or use its established rated design. Tan took that choice back in a letter. Zhu let the mock-up remain on the cold bench while they waited. Jian held it one last time and declared the sitting duck more comfortable than the elegant cup. Han said every duck hoped for such professional recognition.

kiln_p04_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_039.text: Yue helped make ordinary nontrial practice cups while the formal design question travelled. She found the handle harder than the foot. It sagged if attached too wet and separated if the joined surfaces dried unevenly. Zhu showed her how to score and wet the ordinary join without smearing away the intended wall thickness. Yue's first handle held after drying, but looked as though it wanted to crawl back into the cup. Her second was cleaner and cracked at the lower join. Neither entered a retained trial as a secretly successful apprentice contribution.

kiln_p04_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_040.text: Han offered to show her his oldest handle, kept on a shelf behind the tool cupboard. It resembled an ear torn from a frightened animal. He had preserved it because his father laughed and then helped him make another. Yue held it carefully, noticing how few stories about learning arrived in the archive unless somebody intentionally saved them. Failed commercial trials carried dates, costs and witnesses. Failed first attempts often survived only in a maker's private humor. She asked whether he wanted a copy of its outline in her study book. He said yes, but demanded a flattering name.

kiln_p04_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_041.text: They settled on The Listening Vessel, whose ear appeared to have heard terrible news. Zhu laughed at the name and made Yue redraw the join correctly beside it. The page could carry humor and instruction without confusing the two. Yue took it upstairs that evening, where her roommates competed to invent what news the vessel had heard. One suggested the price of charcoal. The other suggested that its maker intended a second ear. Yue laughed until she had to put the pencil down. The day's failed samples had not swallowed every other kind of failure.

kiln_p04_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_042.text: The purchaser's answer rejected the wider handle as too costly for four hundred units. It proposed a smaller introductory run under the established reference design, with the same low price calculated from the original drawing. Tan brought the letter to the owner before making another promise. She asked Zhu and Luo for a real estimate. Zhu counted the ordinary forming time, the additional clay and the separate handle work. Luo counted development and firing space. Their estimate exceeded the purchaser's figure without any secret luxury. A useful object cost what its actual tasks required, not what its first sketch implied.

kiln_p04_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_043.text: The owner offered to accept a properly funded smaller run after the development trial, or decline the commission. She would not pay the difference by cutting apprentice meals or disguising trial labor as free training. Yue heard that sentence with gratitude and unease. It should have been an ordinary boundary, yet she knew places where it would sound extravagant. Peng wrote the offer plainly. Tan looked at the estimate, then added the actual delivery uncertainty himself. He had begun doing work that made the answer harder to sell and easier for the hall to live under.

kiln_p04_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_044.text: At the end of the day, Luo asked Yue to walk the cold hall with him. He wanted another person's view of the clear route, not another reserve reading. She pointed out a low tool box near the handover station and a drip beneath the outer lintel. He moved the box and marked the drip for ordinary repair. Then he stopped at the old scorched door frame. He said he sometimes wanted every new procedure to absolve the younger foreman who had missed a warning years ago. Yue could see how easily improvement became a private bargain with one's past.

kiln_p04_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_045.text: She asked whether the old worker had ever written after leaving. Luo said once, to request a wage statement for another job. He had sent it promptly, along with an offer to answer questions about the burn treatment. The worker had asked for no further conversation. Luo had respected that silence and sometimes resented it. Yue did not offer to find the person and arrange a reconciliation. The archive could improve its account without requiring an injured worker to return and comfort the workshop. They walked past the frame toward the ordinary repair slate.

kiln_p04_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_046.text: Outside, the town was preparing a small winter market. Children tied scrap paper to a fence, and the bakery owner complained that every new decoration collected more soot. Zhu had volunteered to help her friend's daughter braid the bright ribbon. Yue held the comb while Zhu worked slowly with the left hand. The child demanded a loop large enough to see from the alley. Her mother wanted a smaller loop that would survive the wind. They settled on two modest loops. Yue admired an argument resolved by the person who had to wear its result.

kiln_p04_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_047.text: Jian came past carrying a parcel of paid-for household grain. He saw the ribbon and looked away before anyone could invite him to the market. Yue followed him only as far as the gate. He said festivals cost money even when the stalls claimed attendance was free. She offered to walk with him without buying anything. He considered the offer, then said he had promised to send the parcel that evening. They took it to the ordinary carrier together. On the return walk he admitted that he wanted to see the market's cheap wooden toys.

kiln_p04_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_048.text: The toys were carved badly and painted brightly. Jian bought none, but named which his brother would have liked. Yue saw him return twice to a little cart whose axle moved straight. Its maker was an older woman with a blunt knife and excellent patience. She let the boy examine the ordinary join without asking for a purchase. He thanked her with unusual solemnity. Later he sketched that join in his own book. Not every useful lesson needed an institution's register, although the work he did for the kiln deserved its own honest one.

kiln_p04_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_049.text: They watched a puppet show in which a proud magistrate bought a pot that claimed it could judge liars. The pot declared every person a liar except its seller. Han, appearing behind them with a fried cake, said this was the most realistic official in the town. Yue laughed at the magistrate's expensive face. Jian laughed harder when the pot cracked and blamed the table. For a while their shared suspicion of grand promises had a harmless target. Then the puppeteer passed the collection bowl, and each gave a small coin for the actual work they had enjoyed.

kiln_p04_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_050.text: Zhu found them afterward and demanded an account of the show. Jian performed the cracked pot's speech with such accuracy that Han nearly choked on his cake. Tan stood nearby listening, then laughed at the table's supposed fault. Yue had worried the joke would feel directed at him. He said the table should request a written correction and joined the others for the short walk home. Friendship was not acquittal. It was a moment in which nobody needed the clerk to remain only the worst thing he had done that month.

kiln_p04_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_051.text: The next morning the lintel repair began. A carpenter replaced a decayed strip while the kiln remained cold. Yue helped move dry boards out of the falling dust and counted their returned positions afterward. She found a teaching sample tag beneath one board, left from the failed shelf. Its original cup was already archived, so she returned the loose tag to the matching cover rather than tying it to a new vessel. That mistake could have made an old failure look like a new sample result. The repair left them with a tighter door and one recovered scrap of identity.

kiln_p04_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_052.text: Peng asked whether Yue had entered the loose tag discovery. Yue had not yet. She expected another lesson about records. Instead Peng handed her a clean scrap and asked her to be brief. The place, date and restored match were enough. An archive that described every breath would bury the events readers needed to find. Yue wrote three plain lines. Peng approved and returned to an ordinary fuel invoice. The restraint pleased Yue. Care did not require making life into an endless document; it required knowing which small facts might later change an answer.

kiln_p04_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_053.text: The registrar accepted Zhu's final supported update near the end of the week. Zhu showed the complete retrospective transcript to Han, who congratulated her by asking whether she would now charge more for insulting his bowls. She said the fee had always been earned. Luo kept the workshop's corrected procedure copy in the apprenticeship folder. Jian compared it with his own and found the same current fields. The old record had altered a present practice rather than becoming merely a framed apology. Yue felt proud of helping, then remembered that Zhu had set the scope and lived the work.

kiln_p04_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_054.text: She asked Zhu whether she could mention the correction in her next letter home, without the private injury account. Zhu agreed to the institutional part and the completed skill fields. She wanted no sentimental portrait of patience. Yue crossed out an admiring phrase before posting. Her mother would understand the corrected assessment without being told what emotion to attach to another woman's years. The resulting letter was shorter and warmer. It also described the puppet's lying pot, because some true things deserved to travel simply for the pleasure they could give.

kiln_p04_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_055.text: Tan received the association's amended advance receipt. The conditional month was removed, and return terms were made plain while the larger order remained unaccepted. He showed it to the owner and Peng before filing. The suspense balance still matched the original amount. Yue noticed how tired he looked after obtaining the correction. He had spent more effort unwinding one hopeful signature than he would have spent asking the proper question before writing it. He said this himself, bitterly. Peng answered that the correction had arrived before the money was spent. That fact was worth keeping alongside the mistake.

kiln_p04_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_056.text: The association agreed to pay for one redesigned small material trial under the fuller estimate, delaying its large-order decision. Its own specialist would review the release arrangement after ordinary firing, using the established method and new geometry. The kiln owner accepted the funded scope. Luo scheduled it after other paid work, allowing the fresh body enough ordinary drying time. No one promised four hundred vessels before spring. Tan put the new agreement beside the old rejected price, where he could see the difference each time he reached for a blank order sheet.

kiln_p04_057.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_057.text: Zhu made the next trial set with wider feet and handles based on the ordinary mock-up. Yue helped prepare body and record dimensions, then returned to practice pieces while Zhu finished the retained joins. The division hurt her pride for a moment. She wanted a real maker's mark on a sample that mattered. Zhu said the next set needed repeatable known work, while Yue's learning still varied. There was nothing unkind in the answer. Yue made three ordinary practice handles and kept the best for a later assessed exercise instead of sneaking it into the commission.

kiln_p04_058.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_058.text: Jian asked whether she resented being left out. Yue said yes, a little. He was astonished that she admitted it without trying to make the feeling sound noble. She asked whether resentment meant the trial should depend on a handle she could not yet repeat. He conceded it did not. They compared practice pieces, and his new foot was cleaner than hers. She praised it plainly. He looked so pleased that she wondered how often learners lost useful praise because everyone feared it would make them proud. The boy was already proud. Accurate praise gave his pride specific ground.

kiln_p04_059.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_059.text: At the next clinic review, Yue's ordinary grip and shoulder movement remained normal. Her established reserve had improved with settled meals, while the recovered throughput stayed unchanged. The examiner discussed the planned Su Yan visit and recommended keeping the work roster available, including the brief sleep disruption. Yue asked whether admitting that disruption would make a new teacher decline her. The examiner said a teacher who needed a fictional body would be the wrong teacher. Yue smiled. She had heard more elegant instructions, but few she could remember so easily while trying to look capable.

kiln_p04_060.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_060.text: She took the review to Peng, then spent the afternoon cleaning the ordinary comparison room. The reference bench had not been used for new-route work in several months. Dust lay under one removable panel. Yue stopped before lifting the panel because its edge carried the reference seal. Luo opened it under the keeper's entry and found an old uncharged lead with a frayed outer cover. It was replaced, not hidden beneath a cleaner cloth. The room would need calibration before Su Yan considered a plan. Cleaning had discovered a real task, not earned permission by making the floor shine.

kiln_p04_061.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_061.text: Han teased that Yue had managed to create work even for a room that was doing nothing. She replied that his old handle had created a permanent drawing assignment for everyone upstairs. He asked whether the drawing was flattering. She showed him the new caption. The Listening Vessel had acquired a small crown and a worried eyebrow through her roommate's contribution. Han laughed and demanded the crown be removed unless it came with wages. Yue left it in the private joke book, clearly separate from the actual study sketch. Not every useful object needed a sober life.

kiln_p04_062.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_062.text: Rain returned as the month turned. Water rattled on the repaired lintel without entering, and the yard smelled of wet charcoal under its sound cover. Yue helped move dry practice boards to the inner rack. Jian stood beside the relay bell, watching drops collect along its cord. He asked whether a wet cord could change a warning response. Luo arranged a cold check in the actual condition before the next firing. The answer proved acceptable, but the check gave them a place to enter later weather changes. Jian looked pleased to have asked a question before it became a complaint.

kiln_p04_063.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_063.text: Peng brought the old failed shelf packet upstairs for a final material cross-reference. The recent trials had confirmed why fired reclaim particles mattered to thin body, but they had not resolved the old cooling gap or missing relay responsibility. Yue suggested making a new archive section for failures whose causes remained mixed. Peng asked whether that would help readers find related evidence or merely give uncertainty a tidier name. Yue thought before answering. They linked material, geometry, schedule and warning observations separately, with the original failure card retained. Readers could follow several questions without being forced to inherit one verdict.

kiln_p04_064.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_064.text: In the packet's back cover, Yue found an older supplier circular copied to the former keeper. It described a cheaper firing programme intended only for ordinary storage body. A marginal note proposed extending it to thin teaching ware after one promising sample. The proposed extension carried no completed trial result. Tan recognised the circular as the source of a current association estimate. Luo stared at the page. The unsafe promise was not new; it had travelled forward in a respectable file while its missing evidence remained behind. Yue felt the archive's dust become suddenly less remote.

kiln_p04_065.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_065.text: She compared the circular's dates with the new contract draft. The association had reused the old economical schedule as if years of repetition had made it proven. Its reference cup came from a different body and geometry. The current redesigned trial could answer a narrow material question, but the larger proposed production schedule still needed its own development. Tan wanted to send a concise warning immediately. Peng agreed after they checked the copies. Nobody accused the association of knowing what the archive had only just found. They asked it to supply the actual supporting trial record or correct the proposal.

kiln_p04_066.speaker: narrator
kiln_p04_066.text: The hall closed early that evening for an ordinary roof inspection. Yue left with Zhu through the wet yard, carrying her work notes. They stopped beneath the bakery eaves and listened to rain thicken on the street. Zhu said she hoped the next trial would be boring. Yue answered that she had begun to understand boring as a costly skill. They ate warm bread from torn paper and watched a child steer a wooden cart through a puddle. Somewhere under the kiln stairs, an old unproved programme waited to explain how a new impossible price had learned to look familiar.
